mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 4 Series M440i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 4 Series M440i engine replacement typically costs between £3,800 and £6,000 for a reconditioned unit, with rebuilt engines ranging from £5,000 to £8,000. Used engines start from around £2,000. These prices are supply-only - fitting adds 12-16 hours of labour at specialist rates (£780-£1,040) due to the complexity of the B58 engine.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the BMW 4 Series M440i B58 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The B58 engine in the M440i is generally reliable, but there are some well-documented issues to be aware of. The most common are cooling system leaks (plastic vent hoses, water pump seals), oil filter housing and valve cover gasket leaks, and VANOS solenoid failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 4 Series M440i?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a BMW 4 Series M440i valued at £30,000-£60,000, a rebuilt engine at £5,000-£8,000 is typically worthwhile if the car is otherwise in good condition. This represents approximately 10-20% of the vehicle's value.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 4 Series M440i and M440i xDrive?

acceptedAnswer.text: All UK-market BMW 4 Series M440i models are xDrive (all-wheel drive) as standard. The M440i xDrive features BMW's intelligent all-wheel-drive system with rear-biased torque distribution, providing enhanced traction and handling. The engine is identical - the B58B30O1 or B58B30O2 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-six producing 374bhp.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 4 Series M440i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 4 Series M440i engine replacement typically takes 2-4 days for a specialist workshop to complete, assuming the replacement engine is already in stock. The B58's complexity and rear-mounted timing chain design mean the job requires more time than a 4-cylinder engine.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a BMW 4 Series M440i replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every rebuilt and reconditioned engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Some suppliers offer extended warranties of up to 24 months on certain engine types. Always confirm exact terms with your chosen supplier before purchase.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW 4 Series M440i reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 4 Series M440i with the B58 engine is widely regarded as one of BMW's most reliable modern performance engines. The B58 has earned a reputation for robustness and tuning potential. However, like any high-performance engine, it requires diligent maintenance - particularly regular oil changes and cooling system inspections.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 4 Series M440i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW M440i arrived in 2020 as the flagship non-M performance variant of the G22 4 Series range, replacing the 440i. It is powered exclusively by the B58 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-six engine - widely regarded as one of BMW's finest modern powerplants - and is available across all three body styles: Coupe (G22), Convertible (G23) and Gran Coupe (G26), with xDrive all-wheel drive as standard on UK models.

milestones.description: B58B30O1, 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-six petrol, 374bhp / 275kW, 500Nm torque, Euro 6d compliant, 48V mild-hybrid system (MHEV) introduced
B58B30O1 continues; Gran Coupe (G26) M440i xDrive introduced with same powertrain
B58TU2 ("Technical Update 2") engine variant introduced with cylinder deactivation and switchable rocker arms
M440i receives the B58B30O2 (TU2) with revised 48V mild-hybrid system and updated engine calibration
Current generation continues with B58B30O2 engine, producing 374bhp with 48V MHEV assistance

commonProblems.h2: BMW 4 Series M440i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 4 Series M440i is powered by the B58 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-six - one of BMW's most celebrated modern engines. While the B58 is significantly more reliable than its N55 predecessor, it has its own set of well-documented issues, many of which stem from heat management and plastic components in the cooling system. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Cooling System Failures - Plastic Vent Hoses and Water Pump Leaks
problems.rootCause: The B58's cooling system relies on plastic components - vent hoses, quick-release couplers, and water pump seals - that sit close to sustained turbo heat. Heat cycling causes these plastics to crack and fail, leading to slow coolant loss. The intercooler sits inside the intake plenum, packing extra coolant lines against the hottest part of the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cracked vent hose; system flush and refill
repairOptions.longevity: If caught early; prevents further coolant loss

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, thermostat and seals; full coolant system flush
repairOptions.longevity: If water pump seal has failed; prevent overheating

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, includes updated cooling components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If overheating has caused secondary damage; peace of mind with warranty

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A BMW 4 Series M440i of 2020-2025 vintage typically sits in the £30,000-£60,000 value band `[THIRD-PARTY, AutoTrader/Cazoo]`. At this price point, replacement costs are relatively small compared to vehicle value - a rebuilt engine at £5,000-£8,000 represents approximately 10-20% of the car's worth. For most M440i owners, a full rebuilt engine with warranty is financially viable if failure occurs.
problems.recommendation: For the BMW 4 Series M440i, regular cooling system inspections are essential. The plastic vent hose connecting the oil filter housing to the expansion tank is a known weak point - have it inspected at every service, and consider preventative replacement at 60,000 miles. If you notice coolant loss or warning lights, address it immediately to prevent overheating-related engine damage.

problems.group: Oil Filter Housing and Valve Cover Gasket Leaks
problems.h4: Oil Filter Housing and Valve Cover Gasket Leaks
problems.rootCause: The oil filter housing (OFH) and valve cover gaskets are made of rubber that degrades over time due to heat cycling. The OFH can warp or fail internally, while the valve cover gasket hardens and cracks, allowing oil to seep out. The B58's hot-vee design accelerates this degradation.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace gasket; clean oil residue from engine bay
repairOptions.longevity: If oil spots or burning smell present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace OFH and gaskets; oil system flush
repairOptions.longevity: If oil filter housing has warped or failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, includes updated gaskets, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If oil starvation has caused internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: At £30,000-£60,000 vehicle values `[THIRD-PARTY]`, gasket replacement is a minor expense relative to the car's worth. Full engine replacement is rarely required for gasket issues alone - only consider it if oil starvation has caused secondary internal damage.
problems.recommendation: Oil filter housing and valve cover gasket leaks are common on the B58 but are relatively straightforward repairs. Have your BMW 4 Series M440i inspected at every service for signs of oil leaks. If you notice oil spots on your driveway or a burning oil smell, address it promptly - catching these leaks early prevents more serious issues.

problems.h4: VANOS Solenoid Failure - Rough Idle and Power Loss
problems.rootCause: The VANOS solenoid's rubber O-ring degrades due to heat and oil contamination, leading to solenoid failure. This affects the variable valve timing system, resulting in power loss and rough running.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace solenoid and O-ring; reset adaptations
repairOptions.longevity: If rough idle or power loss present; preventive at 50,000 miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, includes updated VANOS components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Only if VANOS failure has caused secondary damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: At £30,000-£60,000 vehicle values `[THIRD-PARTY]`, VANOS solenoid replacement is a minor expense. BMW recommends replacing VANOS seals every 50,000 miles as preventive maintenance.
problems.recommendation: For the BMW 4 Series M440i, VANOS solenoid replacement is a straightforward and relatively inexpensive repair. If you experience rough idle, slow throttle response or power loss, have the VANOS system inspected. Preventive replacement of the VANOS seals at 50,000 miles is recommended by BMW specialists and can prevent unexpected failures.
